description: Thread-safe mutable multi-map for .NET — multiple values per key, implements ILookup for drop-in LINQ interop.
rules: MultiMap<TKey, TValue> is IDisposable — it holds a ReaderWriterLockSlim. Dispose it, or declare it with using, when the map is not a long-lived singleton.
The safe read is TryGetValues (plural), not TryGetValue — it yields the whole collection for the key.
Remove(key, value) drops a single pair; RemoveAll(key) drops every value under the key.
Count is the number of keys. Use ValueCount for the number of pairs.

It implements ILookup<TKey, TValue>, so it can be assigned to an ILookup variable with no conversion and no copy. Use that instead of rebuilding via Enumerable.ToLookup, which produces an immutable snapshot.
Returned collections are snapshots, so enumerating while other threads mutate is safe.
Insertion order is preserved under each key. Duplicates are allowed by default (list semantics); set semantics are opt-in.
Targets netstandard2.0 and has no dependencies.
